Eleventh Indian Expedition to Antarctica, Scientific Report 1995 
Department of Ocean Development, Technical Publication No. 9,, pp. 267-300 
Comparative Performance of Thirty Two Crop s Grown 
in Antarctic Soil, Antarctic Moss and Peat MOSS Under 
Glass House Conditions in Antarctica 
MOHOMMAD ARIF and M.C. JOSHI 
Defence Agricultural Research Laboratory Haldwani - 263 139 
Abstract 
Eighty one varieties of 29 different vegetables, two varieties of grass and one variety 
of maize were grown in three different media viz. Antarctic soil, Antarctic moss and Peat 
moss. Performance of leafy vegetables (Spinach, fenugreek, lettuce, parseley, garlic, onion, 
mint and coriander), cucurbits (cucumber, bittergourd and squash), beans, brinjal, chilli and 
tomato was quite promising. Cruciferous plants (radish, knol khol, turnip, lai, cabbage and 
cauliflower) did not respond well during austral summer. 
Introduction 
The col d desert  o f Antarctica supports onl y a n impoverishe d communit y

of total or near total darkness during whic h period photosynthesi s can no t take

flowerin g plant s (Gree n an d Green , 1963) . Growt h mus t occu r durin g shor t 
summer period which lasts for a few days to a few months dependin g on divers e

is th e mos t importan t singl e variabl e provide d mainl y b y atmospheri c wate r 
vapour and by loca l melt supplies from snow, drift snow and permafrost. Stream 
run-off is exceedingl y rare. Extreme cold, high winds and aridity inhibit growth

(Benton,1980 ) o f whic h 35 0 ar e lichen s an d 10 0 are bryophytes . Numerou s

Materials and Methods 
The glas s hous e i n Maitr i statio n ha s a  total are a o f 27.0 7 m 2 o f whic h

Differen t varietie s o f 2 9 horticultural crop s (wate r melon , mus k melon ,
